- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., > +10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for first 5 days.  
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3), model lags in recognizing trend shift; adjust forecast to align with sentiment reversal within 2–3 days.  
- Mean reversion is overemphasized in model; if price is > 20% above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
